# infinIT.us

US· Cleveland mid

Overview

Account Executive $85,000 – $150,000 OTE (Base + Commission) | Full-Time New Business Development | Cleveland, OH The kind of person we are looking for: Are you energized by opening new doors, not just closing them? Do you lead with curiosity before you lead with a pitch?

New Business Development | Cleveland, OH 

### About the Role

As an Account Executive at infinIT, your job is to grow our client base. You own the full sales process, from first outreach through signed agreement. 

You will prospect, qualify, run discovery, build proposals, and close. You will be the face of infinIT in every early-stage client conversation, and how you show up matters. 

This is a hunter role. If you are most comfortable managing existing relationships, this is probably not the right fit. 

This is also a consultative sale. You will be working with business owners and operators who are often dealing with IT challenges, risk, or uncertainty. Your ability to build trust, ask the right questions, and guide them to the right solution is critical. 

### What We Offer

✓ Base salary + commission structure with on-target earnings between $85,000 and $150,000+

✓ Commission tied to new business revenue

✓ Typical deal sizes and sales cycles will be discussed during the interview process

You are consistently generating qualified opportunities through outbound effort and referrals 

Your pipeline is real, not inflated, not stale 

Prospects feel like they are talking to a trusted advisor, not a vendor 

You forecast accurately and deliver on what you commit to 

You close new business and hand it off cleanly to the service team 

You represent infinIT with professionalism and genuine care 

- You are building consistent pipeline through outbound activity 

- You are running discovery conversations with confidence 

- You are progressing opportunities toward your first closed deals 

### Responsibilities

~1 min read

Proven track record in IT or technology sales in a hunter or new business development role 

Experience selling managed services, cybersecurity, cloud, or related solutions 

Strong communication skills and the ability to build credibility with business decision-makers 

Disciplined pipeline and CRM management 

Genuine curiosity about the businesses you sell to 

Coachable, you want to get better and are open to feedback 

Competitive drive that does not need a spotlight 

Ability to lead consultative, trust-based conversations rather than transactional sales 

On-site role based in Cleveland, OH with regular local travel for client meetings 

This is a self-directed role with clear expectations around activity and outcomes. You will have access to technical and leadership support, but success in this role requires ownership, consistency, and initiative. 

Our team values responsiveness, accountability, and doing what we say we will do for both clients and each other.

# Outbound doesn’t need a 20-tool monster stack to work. | Palash Wadekar🛸 · LinkedIn · 2026-03-06

**Palash Wadekar🛸**: Palash Wadekar currently works as Co-Founder at Growth Infi for 3 years 2 months with 5 years of total professional experience. Previous roles include Sales automation - consultant at Hector, Relationship Manager at Fineappl, and President at Rotaract Club Of Sydenham College. Based in Mumbai, Maharashtra, India [IN].

---

Outbound doesn’t need a 20-tool monster stack to work.

Most teams keep adding software hoping it will magically fix pipeline problems. In reality, complexity just creates more failure points.

A lean system usually wins.

Start with clean data, enrich it with signals, generate relevant context, and run multi-channel outreach that’s easy to monitor and scale.

For us, that looks like: sourcing → enrichment ([Clay](https://linkedin.com/company/grow-with-clay)) → AI-assisted research → email outreach ([Smartlead](https://linkedin.com/company/smartlead-ai))  + LinkedIn outreach (HeyReach.io) → nurturing ([Breakcold](https://linkedin.com/company/breakcold))

Tools like [Clay](https://linkedin.com/company/grow-with-clay), [Smartlead](https://linkedin.com/company/smartlead-ai), and HeyReach make this simple when used in the right sequence.

Keep the stack lean.
Keep the system predictable.

#outbound #sales

60-Day Outbound Pilot: How to Prove Market Signal Before a Large GTM Commitment

 July 27, 2026 · Uncategorized 

# 60-Day Outbound Pilot: How to Prove Market Signal Before a Large GTM Commitment

Surprising fact: the Los Angeles Pilot Service began in 1907 and still relies on nearly 30 professionals to guide vessels safely—proof that skilled teams and strict requirements scale results over time.

Startups can borrow that mindset. A short, structured trial acts like a controlled flight test. It shows whether market signals exist before a major go-to-market commitment.

Federal rules require a commander to log at least 1,500 hours for certain operations, and that same rigor helps founders set clear program requirements. By treating an outreach program like flight training, teams build repeated practice, instrument time, and consistent procedures.

Is Gasimo the right outbound partner for you?

Three fields. Thirty seconds. We only follow up when there is a genuine fit.

In practice, this approach reduces risk, sharpens controls, and gets the company closer to its target destinations—one landing, or sales meeting, at a time. For a practical framework, see a guide on building a strong sales pipeline with strategic outreach at strategic outreach.

### Key Takeaways

- Treat a short trial as a controlled flight to validate market demand.
- Set clear requirements and repeatable procedures before scaling.
- Regular practice mirrors flight training and keeps teams current.
- Use measured instrument time to reduce risk and improve accuracy.
- A focused test helps founders avoid large, costly GTM bets.

## Why Founders Need a 60 Day Outbound Pilot

A condensed outreach test gives teams a way to validate demand without heavy hiring. It acts like a simulated instrument check for a new sales program: quick, controlled, and measurable.

Gasimo positions itself as an outcome-focused partner for high-ACV B2B teams. The company moves clients beyond generic retainers and static lead lists toward qualified replies and sales-ready conversations.

Founders often face a 90-day recruit cycle followed by 30 to 60 months of ramp time for new hires. That slow ramp creates idle salary costs while hires learn the playbook.

- Performance-linked pricing: aligns incentives so outcomes matter.
- Revenue-sharing: reduces upfront risk for founder-led GTM.
- Focused results: qualified replies, accepted SQLs, booked calls.

In short, a small test gives real evidence before a big GTM commitment. For a practical playbook on founder-led outreach, see this guide to building meetings without a full SDR team: founder-led outbound book.

## Defining Your Ideal Customer Profile and Market Signal

When the ideal customer is mapped, teams can focus on signals that predict revenue. This section shows how a clear ICP and visible buyer pain feed a short trial that proves demand.

Identifying visible buyer pain

### Identifying Visible Buyer Pain

Gasimo begins by scanning the market for problems buyers openly discuss. They use public signals, job posts, and product changes to spot decision-makers who feel the pain.

This narrows outreach so messaging lands with the right people. That focus reduces wasted time and improves reply rates.

### Assessing ROI Potential

Before scaling, Gasimo tests whether meetings convert to value. The team models expected pipeline and checks economics against revenue targets.

They require a targetable ICP and clear ROI to hit the program goal of 8 to 15 meetings per SDR. This keeps founders from pouring money into broad lists or blind marketing.

| Criteria | Signal | Why it matters | Early outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Targetable ICP | Company size, role titles | Enables focused outreach | Higher reply rate |
| Visible buyer pain | Product changes, help requests | Shows urgency to buy | Qualified conversations |
| ROI potential | Deal size, sales cycle | Validates spend | Measurable pipeline |

## Structuring the Pilot for Rapid Execution

A compressed ramp lets teams prove motion and start booking qualified meetings almost immediately.

Gasimo builds a short training window and clear controls so SDRs reach production fast. Their SDRs hit full output after a 7-day ramp, not months.

### The Importance of a Short Ramp Period

Speed with structure matters: the 7-day ramp pairs focused training with real outreach. That keeps aircraft-like discipline in messaging and handoffs.

Structured people systems let Gasimo plug into an existing sales stack. That prevents platform migrations and keeps operations steady.

- Fast readiness: teams book meetings within hours of launch.
- Qualification-first: closers get only sales-ready prospects.
- Weekly reviews: iterate cadence based on real reply and meeting-set rates.

| Feature | Why it matters | Expected early outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 7-day ramp | Short training with hands-on outreach | Fast meeting velocity |
| People systems | Seamless integration into current stack | No new licenses or migrations |
| Qualification before handoff | Improves close rates | Higher-quality pipeline |
| Growth-partner plans | Aligns cost with outcomes | Lower upfront risk for founders |

## Integrating Nearshore SDRs into Your Existing Sales Stack

Bringing nearshore SDRs into your stack should feel like adding a skilled co-pilot, not a new aircraft. Gasimo embeds Caribbean SDRs into your existing Outreach, Salesloft, or Apollo setup so teams keep their current sequencer, sales intelligence, and CRM licenses.

This avoids tool rebuilds, migrations, and duplicate seat fees. Data flows stay clean and your CRM remains the single source of truth. That reduces risk and speeds time to first meeting.

### Maintaining Compliance and Data Integrity

Multichannel suppression ledger unifies voice, email, and SMS records. That prevents accidental sends and keeps compliance gaps closed across campaigns.

### Leveraging AI for Quality Assurance

Gasimo runs 100% AI QA on every call. Each conversation is scored against the discovery script and objection handling criteria.

- Daily coaching on the lowest 10% of calls.
- AI checks preserve brand voice and consistent messaging.

### Aligning Time Zones for Maximum Coverage

Caribbean SDRs operate in US Eastern and Central shifts. That alignment covers the hours when prospects are most active and improves contact rates and landings for meetings.

For a practical checklist to start clean, see the fresh start checklist. To learn how Gasimo runs integrated SDR programs, review their SDR offering at SDR pilot service.

## Measuring Success Through Pipeline and Revenue Outcomes

Gasimo measures success by tracking qualified replies, accepted SQLs, booked calls, and sales-ready conversations. The program targets 8 to 15 booked meetings per SDR per month and ties that output to closer feedback in the CRM.

Real-time visibility matters. Success is counted by sales-accepted meetings and the opp-creation rate, visible in your CRM the moment a meeting is logged. Gasimo also offers a live meeting and pipeline dashboard so your VP of Sales can watch progress alongside internal teams.

- ICP-fit scoring on every booked meeting keeps the pipeline revenue-ready.
- Weekly pipeline reviews with RevOps allow fast iteration on meeting-set rates and downstream quality.
- The program ends with a clear revenue assessment, giving founders evidence to justify a larger GTM commitment.

For guidance on scaling measurement and operations, see Gasimo’s logistics pipeline playbook or explore growth consulting to align outcomes with your sales model: logistics pipeline playbook and growth consulting.

## Conclusion

A focused, measurable trial turns assumptions into facts you can act on. Founders get low-risk evidence that their market exists without long hiring cycles. Gasimo’s team pairs nearshore SDRs with AI-driven QA and stack-native integration to speed results and keep data clean.

Measure by concrete metrics — qualified replies, sales-accepted meetings, and pipeline value. This approach saves time and compresses learnings into a few days so teams can decide with confidence.

Start a small pilot to prove fit, log meaningful landings in the CRM, and scale only when metrics justify the move. Learn frameworks for ABM testing at ABM pilot programme or streamline scheduling with Gasimo’s playbooks at scheduling playbooks.

### What is the goal of a 60-day outbound pilot?

The goal is to validate market demand quickly with a focused outreach program that proves buyers respond to the offer before investing in a full go-to-market rollout. It tests messaging, target segments, and sales motions to generate measurable pipeline and revenue signals within a short timeframe.

### Who should run this pilot within a startup?

Founders or head of sales usually lead the effort, with support from SDRs, marketing, and customer success. Nearshore SDRs can be integrated to scale outreach while the core team monitors results and refines targeting and value propositions.

### How is the ideal customer profile (ICP) defined for the pilot?

The team defines ICP by combining firmographics, technographics, and visible buyer pain. They prioritize accounts with clear ROI potential and buying signals, then build a list that supports rapid testing of messaging and channels.

### What counts as a visible buyer pain?

Visible buyer pain includes publicly stated problems, regulatory pressures, or recurring job postings that indicate need. These signals suggest a higher likelihood of engagement and faster path to meaningful conversations and demos.

### How long should ramp-up be before full outreach begins?

Ramp-up should be short—typically a few days to two weeks—to align messaging, confirm data quality, and train SDRs. Short ramps preserve momentum and let the team iterate quickly based on early replies and meeting outcomes.

### How do nearshore SDRs fit into the existing sales stack?

Nearshore SDRs work within the startup’s CRM, cadences, and meeting booking processes. They follow established scripts, log activity, and hand off qualified leads to sales reps. This approach keeps operations consistent while leveraging cost and time-zone advantages.

### What compliance and data integrity measures are required?

The team must enforce data handling policies, secure CRM access, and follow GDPR, CCPA, and other relevant rules. Regular audits and role-based permissions help maintain integrity and protect customer data during the pilot.

### How can AI be used for quality assurance during the pilot?

AI tools can monitor call quality, score outreach messages, and flag noncompliant language. They help managers identify coaching opportunities and ensure consistent messaging across reps while reducing manual review time.

### Why is time-zone alignment important for outbound efforts?

Aligning time zones increases contact rates and enables live conversations during business hours. Nearshore teams often provide extended coverage for North American markets, improving meeting conversion and accelerating sales cycles.

### Which metrics determine pilot success?

Primary metrics include qualified meetings, pipeline value, conversion rates, and early revenue influenced by pilot activities. Secondary metrics track response rates, cadence effectiveness, and data quality for scaling decisions.

### How should results inform a larger GTM commitment?

Results guide whether to scale headcount, adjust messaging, or change target segments. A clear, positive market signal—consistent pipeline growth and predictable conversion—justifies broader investment in sales and marketing.

### What common pitfalls should teams avoid?

Teams should avoid long ramp times, poor data hygiene, unclear qualification criteria, and ignoring compliance. They should also prevent overreliance on a single channel and ensure continuous coaching for SDRs to maintain performance.

### How much outbound volume is necessary to prove signal?

Volume depends on target account list size and conversion targets. Teams aim for enough touches to produce statistically meaningful outcomes—typically hundreds of touches across diversified accounts—to validate messaging and ICP assumptions.

### Can this pilot validate pricing and packaging?

Yes. Early sales conversations reveal price sensitivity and feature priorities. The team can test simple pricing variations and packaging concepts to see what resonates and what accelerates purchasing decisions.

### How often should the team iterate during the pilot?

Iteration should be weekly, with rapid tweaks to messaging, cadences, and targeting based on live data. Frequent standups and data reviews help the team optimize before committing to larger-scale execution.

# Almost six months ago, I entered the world of GTM Engineering. | Lokesh Nagar · LinkedIn · 2026-07-16

**Lokesh Nagar**: Sales And Marketing Intern at Growth Infi for 6 months with 2 years 5 months of total professional experience. Previous roles include Onsite Medical Representative at DERMAYOUTH LIMITED, Ecommerce - Dropshipping & Clothing Brand at Freelance, and Affiliate Marketing at Bizgurukul. Based in Mumbai, Maharashtra, India [IN].

---

Almost six months ago, I entered the world of GTM Engineering.

At first, I thought GTM was mainly about finding leads and sending cold emails.

But I was wrong.

Over the last few months at [Growth Infi](https://linkedin.com/company/growthinfi), I've realized that GTM is much broader than outbound.

It's about creating systems that help businesses grow in a predictable way.

Behind every successful outbound campaign lies more than just a good email.

It involves understanding:

• Who your ideal customer really is
• How to build high-quality prospect lists
• Enriching data before outreach
• Personalizing messages with AI
• Setting up scalable outbound infrastructure
• Maintaining email deliverability
• Automating repetitive workflows
• Continuously testing and improving every step of the process

I've had the chance to work with tools like Clay, Apollo, Smartlead, n8n, OpenAI, LinkedIn Sales Navigator and many more.

One thing these six months have taught me is that tools don't create results.

The system behind them does.

One lesson that has stuck with me is this:

The best GTM teams don’t depend on hustle; they depend on well-designed systems.

This is my first post about GTM, and going forward, I'll share what I'm learning, the workflows I'm building, the experiments I'm running, and lessons that can help anyone interested in modern B2B growth.

Still learning.

Still experimenting.

Still building.

I look forward to connecting with more people in the GTM, RevOps, and AI space.

#GTM #GTMEngineering #RevOps #B2B #Outbound #AI #Automation #SalesTech #Growth
